summary: The note surveys the rise of eco-art, a movement that fuses aesthetics with environmental activism, and profiles emerging artists and projects from September 2023 to July 2024. It covers works that combine art with science, community-driven initiatives, public interventions, and new grants and institutions supporting the genre. The main point is that eco-art actively engages with nature and aims to drive behavioral and environmental change.
one_line: Overview of the eco-art movement, profiling artists, projects, grants and institutions from 2023-2024 that use art to promote environmental awareness and action.
key_facts: Eco-art gained noticeable momentum after September 2023 and actively engages with and affects nature rather than merely representing it.
Marina DeBris makes art from ocean refuse, and Jason deCaires Taylor creates underwater sculptures that serve as artificial reefs.
Jonathan Green unveiled his 'Reforestation Imaginaria' series on September 14, 2023, planting thousands of saplings in urban spaces to boost urban biodiversity.
Zoe Ambrose, a bio-art pioneer, revealed her 'Living Canvas' series on October 3, 2023, using algae as a natural paint that detoxifies air and shows air quality through changes in color and texture.
Samuel Chen and Lisa Huang launched 'Plasticity' on November 5, 2023, with sculptures from recycled plastic waste, each with a digital counter of plastic saved from landfills.
Alicia Escott's 'Biodegradable Futures' opened December 1, 2023, with time-lapse footage of compostable artworks disintegrating in various ecosystems.
Michael Rajzman's 'Thermochromatic Metamorphoses,' displayed since January 12, 2024, uses heat-sensitive paint to depict rising Earth temperatures.
Diana Liu's 'Seed Bomb Garden' launched February 6, 2024, inviting communities to make seed bombs of clay, compost and native plant seeds for neglected urban areas.
Marcus Young and Sofia Alvarez have led the 'Upcycle Hub' participatory workshops since March 11, 2024, teaching people to repurpose everyday materials.
Carlos Gomez's 'Waterprints' debuted April 15, 2024, using water-sensitive papers that reveal hidden messages in rain to raise awareness of water scarcity.
Georgia Fletcher's 'Carbon Footprint Mosaics' (May 2, 2024) are made from sustainable materials and map the carbon footprint of various activities.
The 'EcoVisionaries' grant, instituted June 22, 2024, supports site-specific installations that resolve local environmental issues.
The Green Art Space museum was inaugurated on July 14, 2024, dedicating exhibitions and educational programs to ecological art.
